title: Traceable selenium-doped microplastics and nanoplastics with environmentally realistic morphologies for multi-modal detection in complex biological matrices
content: The detection of microplastics and nanoplastics (MNPs) pollution in environmental studies remains analytically challenging, especially at the nanoscale, due to their small size and low concentrations. Traceable MNPs containing elemental dopants have emerged as an interesting strategy for studying particle fate using element-specific techniques such as inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) and single particle ICP-MS (spICP-MS). However, most existing traceable MNPs rely on model spherical particles that do not reflect the morphological diversity of environmental MNPs. In this work, we produce selenium-doped polystyrene MNPs with environmentally relevant, heterogeneous morphologies by combining free-radical polymerization with cryomilling. Selenium was selected as a tracer due to its low environmental background, its content tunability, its detectability by ICP-MS and the ability to covalently incorporate it into polymer matrices to minimize leaching. To demonstrate the applicability of the traceable particles for biological fate studies, we exposed Daphnia magna to Se-doped MNP suspensions to confirm particle internalization. Time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (ToF-SIMS) provided sub-micrometer localization of Se and polymer fragments within D. magna tissues, while optical photothermal infrared (O-PTIR) spectroscopy provided further verification of the identity and localization of the MNPs. This work introduces a proof-of-concept of an environmentally relevant platform for traceable MNPs and expands the toolbox for studying the fate, transport, and biological interactions of MNPs in controlled environmental systems.
